column1: # Altered copies of ../accepted-proof: at least one row for each sort of item that the format's walker tells apart in
# ivk/key.bin, ivk/leaf/0.bin and example.proof (not one for every field of every round), and some rows for example.req and example.y.
# The columns are those of altered_copies.tsv, whose first lines explain them. Give this file to
# try_altered_copies.py as its third argument.
# Each row names its place by a byte's number or as the file's end, so the table fits the stored
# files alone: on any other file a row's "put NEW over OLD" finds other bytes, and the script stops
# before it tries any copy.
# A description begins with the row's number: K for ivk/key.bin, E for ivk/leaf/0.bin, P for
# example.proof, R for example.req, Y for example.y. A number that is left out stands for a sort
# of item that this configuration does not have.
# In a description, (field "NAME") is the item's name in the list that
# "cp_verify -plan request ... -fields" prints, and rounds are counted from 1 within a chain.
K01: the file's last byte: the last given digest of the opening of tree number 8 of the second chain after round 16 BASE of the second chain: its highest bit flipped
K02: the anchor's root, which the commitment ID covers: the highest bit of its last byte flipped
K03: an element of a prover's message: the first of round 6 PSC epsilon of the one-time chain (field "ranges: bytes, tie: hiding sum"): the lowest bit of its first word flipped
K04: an element in the middle of a long message: round 16 BASE of the second chain (field "a request's own test, last stage: masked message and randomness"): the lowest bit of its first word flipped
K05: an answer to an out-of-domain sample: the first of round 2 SEND answer of the one-time chain: the lowest bit of its third word flipped
K06: a root that the prover sends: round 1 SEND seed of the one-time chain (field "masks of the committer's rows on the table: root"): the highest bit of its last byte flipped
K07: the 32 random bytes of the one-time chain: the lowest bit of the first byte flipped
K08: between the one-time chain and the shared chain: the slot of the one-time chain's seal in its binding tree (one word): 1 for 0
K09: between the one-time chain and the shared chain: the salt of the slot's leaf in the binding tree of the one-time chain's seal: the highest bit of its last byte flipped
K10: an opened symbol of the anchor: the first symbol of the first column in the opening of the anchor after round 4 LOC of the shared chain: its lowest bit flipped
K11: an opened leaf's salt: that of the first column in the opening of tree number 1 of the one-time chain after round 3647 CS of the one-time chain: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
K12: a given digest: the first of the opening of tree number 1 of the one-time chain after round 3647 CS of the one-time chain: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
K13: a nonce: that of round 3647 CS of the one-time chain: its lowest bit flipped
K15: a word that encodes no element: the third word of the last element of round 16 BASE of the second chain written as p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1
K16: the file's first four bytes, which say its kind: a leaf file's (CPEN) for a key file's (CPIK)
K17: the file without its last byte
K18: one zero byte after the file's end
K19: an opened symbol of one of the chain's own trees: the first in the opening of tree number 1 of the one-time chain after round 3647 CS of the one-time chain: its lowest bit flipped
K20: a word that encodes no element: the last opened symbol of the opening of tree number 8 of the second chain after round 16 BASE of the second chain written as 2^64 - 1
K21: the version word: H811 for H821
K22: a stored answer of the anchor's record: the first, right after the root: the lowest bit of its first word flipped
K23: an opened leaf's salt: that of the first column in the opening of the anchor after round 4 LOC of the shared chain: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
K24: a given digest: the first of the opening of the anchor after round 4 LOC of the shared chain: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
E01: the file's last byte: the last given digest of the opening of tree number 2 of the link's chain after round 24 BASE of the link's chain: its highest bit flipped
E02: the leaf table's root, which is in the statement of the link's chain: the highest bit of its last byte flipped
E03: an element of a prover's message: the first of round 7 FOLD epsilon of the link's chain (field "the two folded rows, stage 1: hiding sum"): the lowest bit of its first word flipped
E04: an element in the middle of a long message: round 24 BASE of the link's chain (field "the two folded rows, last stage: masked message and randomness"): the lowest bit of its first word flipped
E05: an opened symbol of the anchor: the first symbol of the first column in the opening of the anchor after round 4 LINK of the link's chain: its lowest bit flipped
E06: an opened symbol of the leaf table: the last symbol of the last column in the opening of the leaf table after round 4 LINK of the link's chain: its lowest bit flipped
E07: a nonce: that of round 4 LINK of the link's chain: its lowest bit flipped
E09: the file's first four bytes, which say its kind: a key file's (CPIK) for a leaf file's (CPEN)
E10: the file without its last byte
E11: an answer to an out-of-domain sample: the first of round 3 SEND answer of the link's chain: the lowest bit of its third word flipped
E12: a root that the prover sends: round 2 SEND seed of the link's chain (field "link: root"): the highest bit of its last byte flipped
E13: the 32 random bytes of the link's chain: the lowest bit of the first byte flipped
E14: an opened leaf's salt: that of the first column in the opening of the anchor after round 4 LINK of the link's chain: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
E15: a given digest: the first of the opening of the anchor after round 4 LINK of the link's chain: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
E16: a word that encodes no element: the third word of the last element of round 24 BASE of the link's chain written as p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1
E17: one zero byte after the file's end
E18: an opened symbol of one of the chain's own trees: the first in the opening of tree number 0 of the link's chain after round 15 CS of the link's chain: its lowest bit flipped
E19: a word that encodes no element: the last opened symbol of the opening of tree number 2 of the link's chain after round 24 BASE of the link's chain written as 2^64 - 1
E20: the version word: H811 for H821
E21: a stored answer of the leaf table's record: the first, right after the root: the lowest bit of its first word flipped
E22: an opened leaf's salt: that of the first column in the opening of the leaf table after round 4 LINK of the link's chain: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
E23: an opened leaf's salt: that of the first column in the opening of tree number 0 of the link's chain after round 15 CS of the link's chain: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
E24: a given digest: the first of the opening of the leaf table after round 4 LINK of the link's chain: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped

P01: first chain, round 6407 REPLY: an element of a prover's message (an element of E: three words): the next token: its first word 199 written as 199 + p (p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1): the same value in an encoding that is not canonical
P02: slot: the request's slot in its batch (one word): 28 written as 28 + 2^6 = 92: its low 6 bits are the true slot
P03: first chain, round 1666 LOC: the round's nonce: another nonce that also gives the 20 bits of proof of work
P04: first chain, round 104 PSC round: an element of a prover's message (an element of E: three words): its first word plus 1
P05: first chain, round 5 PSC epsilon: an element of a prover's message (an element of E: three words): its first word written as p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1, which encodes no element
P06: first chain, round 1 SEND seed: a root that the prover sends: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
P07: first chain, round 2 SEND answer: an answer to an out-of-domain sample (an element of E: three words): its first word plus 1
P08: first chain: the chain's 32 random bytes: the lowest bit of the first byte flipped
P09: first chain, round 6407 REPLY: an element of a prover's message (an element of E: three words): the next token: 200 for 199 (example.y unchanged)
P10: first chain, round 8021 BASE: an element of a prover's message (an element of E: three words): its first word plus 1
P11: first chain, round 1666 LOC: a symbol of an opened column (an element of F: one word), tree number 0 of the first chain, position 1542: plus 1
P12: first chain, round 1666 LOC: an opened leaf's salt, tree number 0 of the first chain, position 1542: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
P13: first chain, round 1666 LOC: a given digest of an opening, tree number 0 of the first chain, at depth 18: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
P14: shared chain, round 4 LOC: a symbol of an opened column (an element of F: one word), leaf table 0, position 169834: plus 1
P15: slot: the salt of the slot's leaf in the batch's binding tree: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
P16: slot: a digest of the slot's path in the batch's binding tree (the last one, a child of the root): the highest bit of its last byte flipped
P17: second chain, round 16 BASE: the round's nonce: plus 1
P18: second chain: the chain's 32 random bytes: the highest bit of the last byte flipped
P19: head: the number of the leaf table on which the proof was made: plus 1 (ivk/leaf/ holds no leaf file of that number)
P20: head: the version word: H811 for H821
P21: head: the file's first four bytes, which say its kind: a leaf file's (CPEN) for a proof file's (CPPF)
P22: second chain, round 16 BASE: a given digest of an opening, tree number 24 of the second chain, at depth 5: the file's last byte: its highest bit flipped
P23: the file without its last byte
P24: one zero byte after the file's end
P25: shared chain, round 4 LOC: an opened leaf's salt, leaf table 0, position 169834: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
P26: shared chain, round 4 LOC: a given digest of an opening, leaf table 0, at depth 23: the lowest bit of its first byte flipped
R01: the request: r, the place of the prompt's last token: 59 for 60: the call would be about one token more (token 60) than the proof is
R02: the request: token 0, a token of the prompt: 244 for 243
R03: the request: e, the end of the checked positions: 65 for 64: more than the 64 tokens that a request has
R04: the request: its last token: 512 for 346: the vocabulary's size, the first number that is no token
Y01: the next token: 200 for 199 (request and proof unchanged)
Y02: the next token: 512 for 199: the vocabulary's size, the first number that is no token
Y03: the token file: four zero bytes after the next token
